summary.short: Creates the Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act (6 Del. C. ch. 12D). It gives Delaware residents rights to access, correct, delete and obtain a portable copy of personal data, and imposes duties on controllers and processors. Takes effect 1 January 2025 or 2026, depending on enactment date.
summary.long: Creates the Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act (6 Del. C. ch. 12D). Residents gain rights to confirm and access, correct, delete and obtain a portable copy of their personal data, to learn recipients, and to opt out of targeted advertising, sale, and solely automated profiling with legal or similarly significant effects. Controllers must respond within 45 days (extendable by 45), provide an appeal, honor authorized agents and opt-out preference signals, limit collection and purposes, obtain consent for sensitive data and for certain minors' data, post a privacy notice, and not discriminate against consumers who exercise rights. Processors must follow controller instructions and meet contract terms. Controllers handling data of 100,000 or more consumers must document data protection assessments for high-risk processing. Coverage: persons doing business in Delaware or targeting residents that process data of 35,000 or more consumers (or 10,000 plus over 20 percent of gross revenue from data sales); excludes state bodies, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA data and other listed categories. The Department of Justice alone enforces, after a notice of violation with at least 60 days to cure; no private right of action is created. Takes effect 1 January 2025 if enacted on or before 1 January 2024, otherwise 1 January 2026.
